# Adjudication Task — Chapter 670

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃670화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|짧지만 긴 시간이었다.
  6|
  7|촌각(寸刻)이 칠주야(七晝夜)처럼 느껴질 만큼.
  8|
  9|지난 수십여 년의 세월을 하나하나 되짚으며 걷고, 산고를 견디지 못해 숨이 끊인 어미의 품에서 울던 핏덩이가 훌쩍 자라나 헌앙한 청년이 되는 것을 지켜볼 수 있을 만큼.
 10|
 11|이렇듯 백상의 고민은 짧으면서도 길었고, 길면서도 짧았다.
 12|
 13|그리고 굳게 닫혀 있던 그의 입술이 침묵을 깨트리며 움직였을 때, 고민에 대한 답은 이미 나와 있었다.
 14|
 15|“후회할 겁니다.”
 16|
 17|야수묘왕이 담담하게 되물었다.
 18|
 19|“무엇을 말하는 것이냐. 너를 찾아온 것을? 아니면 진태경을 비롯한 다른 한족들을 구출한 것을?”
 20|
 21|“지금까지의 모든 것을.”
 22|
 23|“백상, 너처럼 말이냐?”
 24|
 25|“다릅니다.”
 26|
 27|백상이 굳은 얼굴로 말을 이었다.
 28|
 29|“저와 달리 궁주께는 아직 기회가 남아 있습니다. 실수를 되돌릴 수 있는 마지막 기회가.”
 30|
 31|“마지막 기회라…….”
 32|
 33|“이대로 조용히 돌아가신다면, 이 자리에서 보고 들은 것들은 모두 잊겠습니다. 마치 아무 일도 없던 것처럼.”
 34|
 35|“어찌 손바닥으로 하늘을 가릴까. 뇌옥을 지키던 네 수하들을 살려 두라 말했을 때부터 이미 각오하고 있었다.”
 36|
 37|“그들에게 함구하라 명령한다면 따를 것입니다. 저를 향한 백족의 충심(忠心) 또한 궁주께서 거느리신 칠묘호에 지지 않으니.”
 38|
 39|“그것이…… 네가 보일 수 있는 의형제로서의 마지막 정이냐?”
 40|
 41|묵묵히 고개를 끄덕이는 백상을 향해, 야수묘왕은 서글픈 웃음을 지어 보였다.
 42|
 43|“그럼 그 마지막 정에 기대어 다시 한번 부탁하마. 반 시진. 반 시진만이라도 그들을 위해 길을 열어 주어라.”
 44|
 45|“궁주!”
 46|
 47|“설령 돌이킬 수 있다 해도, 돌이키지 않겠다. 그것이 평생을 함께한 우리의 유일한 차이점이지.”
 48|
 49|“……!”
 50|
 51|백상의 눈꼬리가 파르르 떨렸다.
 52|
 53|지금 이 순간 그는 온 힘을 다해 부정하고 싶었다. 당신의 말은 틀렸다고. 당신과 달리 내 앞에는 단 하나의 길만 놓여 있었고, 그 길을 걸을 수밖에 없었다고.
 54|
 55|그러나 이미 굳게 다물어진 입술은 열리지 않았고, 그의 손은 어느덧 검자루에 닿아 있었다.
 56|
 57|철컥. 스르릉.
 58|
 59|짧은 적막을 베어 가르는 서늘한 마찰음. 애검을 늘어트린 백상의 모습을 바라보는 야수묘왕의 눈빛이 깊게 가라앉았다.
 60|
 61|“그래. 그것이 네 선택이냐?”
 62|
 63|“어쩔 수 없소, 궁주. 지금의 내게는…… 이것만이 최선이니까.”
 64|
 65|“어설픈 존대를 듣지 않아도 되니 한결 낫군. 마치 오래전으로 돌아간 것 같아.”
 66|
 67|“궁주도 알고 있지 않소. 우리는 두 번 다시 그 시절로 돌아갈 수 없다는 것을.”
 68|
 69|“그리 생각하느냐?”
 70|
 71|“물론.”
 72|
 73|그 단호한 대답에 야수묘왕은 희미하게 웃었고, 결단을 내린 백상은 망설이지 않았다.
 74|
 75|츠츠츠츠!
 76|
 77|온 사방을 밝히는 휘황한 빛무리. 검강(劍罡)이라 불리는 아득한 기의 집합체가, 목표를 향해 떨어져 내렸다.
 78|
 79|서걱!
 80|
 81|
 82|
 83|* * *
 84|
 85|
 86|
 87|눈처럼 새하얀 백호를 필두로 세 마리의 호랑이는 바람처럼 달려 나갔다.
 88|
 89|칠묘호의 맏이, 원후(猿猴)는 이미 어둠 너머로 사라진 그들의 뒷모습을 바라보며 중얼거렸다.
 90|
 91|“어따, 빠르다.”
 92|
 93|소감은 그것이 전부였다.
 94|
 95|떠날 이들은 떠났고, 남은 이들은 남았다. 그를 비롯한 다른 이들은 후자가 되기를 스스로 선택했을 뿐이다.
 96|
 97|“흐흐.”
 98|
 99|원후는 후련한 웃음과 함께 품 안에서 호리병을 꺼냈다.
100|
101|퐁.
102|
103|마개를 따기 무섭게 퍼져 나가는 주향. 주위에 있던 묘족 전사들이 동시에 눈을 빛냈다.
104|
105|“오호.”
106|
107|“주향 한번 끝내주네. 대형께서 직접 담근 겁니까?”
108|
109|“허어, 개새끼들만 모아 놨나. 왜 이리들 코가 좋아?”
110|
111|입으로는 투덜거려도 눈은 웃고 있다. 원후는 어쩔 수 없다는 듯이 모여든 이들에게 호리병을 돌렸다.
112|
113|“어쩔 수 없군. 얼마 안 되니까 돌아가면서 조금씩 마셔라.”
114|
115|“내 맹세컨대, 대형 입에는 술 한 방울도 안 들어갈 거요.”
116|
117|“아, 이건 못 참지.”
118|
119|껄껄 웃은 묘족 전사들은 순서대로 호리병을 기울였다.
120|
121|가뜩이나 술 좋아하기로 유명한 남만인들. 그것도 장정이 스물이나 되니 술 한 방울 안 남을 거라는 호언장담은 상당한 신빙성이 있었다.
122|
123|하지만…….
124|
125|“크으, 좋다. 이제 대형 차례요. 내 예의상 몇 방울 남겨 뒀지.”
126|
127|마침내 호리병을 받아 든 원후는 피식 웃고 말았다.
128|
129|찰랑.
130|
131|작게 흔들어 본 것만으로도 알 수 있었다. 호리병 안의 술이 채 반도 비워지지 않았다는 것을.
132|
133|술맛이 좋다며 뻔뻔하게 너스레를 떨고 있는 녀석들을 보고 있자니 실소가 절로 흘러나왔다.
134|
135|“이거 알고 보니, 개새끼들이 아니라 순 허풍쟁이들이었군.”
136|
137|“음? 그게 무슨 소리요?”
138|
139|“그러게. 나이 오십 줄에 벌써부터 노망이라도 나셨나?”
140|
141|“헛소리 그만하고 들기나 하시오.”
142|
143|주위의 성화에 원후는 호리병을 기울였다. 자신의 입 안이 아니라, 잡초가 무성하게 자라 있는 땅을 향해.
144|
145|주르륵.
146|
147|“한 방울도 아까워하지 마라. 살아남는다면 모두가 둘러앉아 밤새도록 술잔을 기울일 테고, 이 자리에서 쓰러진다면 죽어서도 취할 수 있을 테니.”
148|
149|“……!”
150|
151|“……!”
152|
153|굳은 얼굴로 그 모습을 지켜보던 이들이 슬쩍 입꼬리를 끌어올렸다.
154|
155|“그래, 그거 좋지.”
156|
157|“대형께서 뭘 좀 아시네.”
158|
159|“하긴, 전부터 무공보다는 술에 더 미쳐 있긴 했지. 안 그런가?”
160|
161|원후도 웃고, 그와 일평생을 함께한 칠묘호도 웃고, 위험한 임무에 기꺼이 자원한 묘족 전사들도 웃었다.
162|
163|후회? 추호도 없다.
164|
165|설령 모두가 이 자리에서 죽는다 하더라도, 그들의 유일한 희망은 살아남아 위험을 빠져나갈 테니까.
166|
167|그렇기에 원후는 기꺼이 웃을 수 있었다.
168|
169|언제나 모든 일에 앞장섰으며, 솔선수범을 위해 당신의 하나뿐인 후계자마저 이곳으로 보낸 한 사람을 떠올리며.
170|
171|‘명령을 어긴 죄는…… 훗날 저승에서 달게 받겠습니다, 주군.’
172|
173|야수묘왕은 물론 야율목 역시 죽음을 두려워하지 않는다.
174|
175|그들은 수하를 방패를 내세우지도, 그렇다고 겁에 질려 뒷걸음질 치지도 않았다.
176|
177|야수묘왕은 늘그막에 얻은 하나뿐인 자식을 세상 그 무엇보다 사랑하지만, 원후가 한 짓을 안다면 호통을 칠 것이다. 목숨에는 귀천(貴賤)이 없다면서.
178|
179|‘그래, 그거면 충분하지. 목숨을 바치는 이유는.’
180|
181|내심 중얼거린 원후는 텅 빈 호리병을 탈탈 털었다.
182|
183|그리고 개미 눈물만큼 떨어지는 술을 바라보며 입맛을 다시다가, 이내 사방에 내려앉은 어둠 어딘가를 향해 불쑥 입을 열었다.
184|
185|“거, 술 좀 있소?”
186|
187|나직한 대답이 들려왔다.
188|
189|“근무 중인 것으로 아는데.”
190|
191|“다 아는 처지에 뭘. 호랑이 좆이나 까 잡수쇼.”
192|
193|원후는 씩 웃었다.
194|
195|이미 예정되어 있던 교대 시간은 한참이나 지났고, 어둠 너머에서 뻗어 나오는 기파는 소름이 끼칠 정도로 강대했다.
196|
197|“그래서, 안 줄 생각이신가?”
198|
199|“묘족에 술 좋아하는 원숭이가 하나 있다는 소리는 들었지. 받게.”
200|
201|휘익.
202|
203|원후는 어둠을 가르며 날아든 물체를 잡아챘다. 그리고 동시에 투박하지만 익숙한 호리병을 확인하고 자신도 모르게 침음성을 흘렸다.
204|
205|“이건…….”
206|
207|틀림없다. 다름 아닌 자신의 주군, 야수묘왕이 직접 만들어 항상 지니고 다녔던 바로 그 호리병이다.
208|
209|“눈에 익은가?”
210|
211|그 순간 귓가를 파고드는 누군가의 목소리. 천천히 고개를 든 원후의 시야에 한 사람이 들어왔다.
212|
213|주인을 알 수 없는 피와 오물로 더럽혀진 백의(白衣). 창백하다는 표현이 어울릴 만큼 새하얀 피부.
214|
215|“……백상.”
216|
217|백상이 건조한 음성으로 답했다.
218|
219|“일개 전사 따위가, 감히 대족장의 이름을 함부로 입에 담는가.”
220|
221|“주군께서는…… 어찌 되셨지?”
222|
223|“곧 알게 될 것이다.”
224|
225|스륵. 파파팟!
226|
227|순식간에 벌어진 일이었다.
228|
229|백상이 피에 젖은 옷소매를 흔들자, 짙은 어둠 속에서 못 잡아도 일백이 넘는 백족 전사들이 나타나 그들을 포위한 것은.
230|
231|‘빌어먹을.’
232|
233|내심 욕설을 중얼거린 원후는 허리춤에 꽂아두었던 박도(朴刀)를 뽑아 들었다.
234|
235|힐끗 하늘을 바라보니 오늘따라 구름에 달이 가려져 있다. 죽기에는 영 좋지 않은 날이었지만, 한편으로는 다행인 일이다.
236|
237|달빛이 어두운 날 벌어지는 추격전에서는 도망자가 유리하니까.
238|
239|‘부디 살아계셔야 합니다, 두 분 모두.’
240|
241|이제 남은 것은 하나뿐이다.
242|
243|원후는, 아니 모두는 망설임 없이 병장기를 들고 적들을 향해 달려나갔다.
244|
245|두려움 따위는 범접할 수도 없을 만큼 거대한 함성과 함께.
246|
247|
248|
249|* * *
250|
251|
252|
253|쐐애애애액!
254|
255|전신을 스치는 바람이 차갑다.
256|
257|지금 이 순간에도 빠르게 스쳐 지나가는 풍경 속에는 사람의 그림자도, 여러 가지 독특한 형태를 띤 가옥(家屋)도 없었고 오직 풀숲만이 가득했다. 어느덧 외궁(外弓)을 벗어난 것이다.
258|
259|‘하지만 아직도 남만야수궁의 영역이다. 속도를 늦춰서는 안 돼.’
260|
261|아니, 어쩌면 척후대에 포함된 화룡각 대원들을 구하기 전까지 쉼 없이 달려야 할지도 모른다.
262|
263|남만야수궁의 힘은 숲과 평야, 밀림과 늪으로 가득한 이 미지의 땅 전체를 아우르니까.
264|
265|“미안하지만 조금만 더 부탁한다.”
266|
267|그르릉.
268|
269|야율목의 말처럼 역시 영물은 영물이다. 세찬 바람 소리 속에서도 용케 내 말을 알아들은 듯, 낮은 울음소리를 흘린 백호가 한층 속도를 높였다.
270|
271|파파파팟!
272|
273|아마 녀석이 이렇게까지 내 말을 잘 따르는 데는, 분명 자신의 등에 묶여 있는 주인의 존재도 한몫했을 것이다.
274|
275|나는 백호가 나아갈 때마다 작게 흔들리는 신형을 바라보며 한숨을 내쉬었다.
276|
277|‘야율목.’
278|
279|정신없이 달리는 사이 외궁을 벗어났지만, 나는 야율목을 깨우지 않았다.
280|
281|아니, 시도하지 못했다고 하는 것이 옳은 표현일 것이다.
282|
283|‘정신을 차린다면 어떻게든 돌아가려고 하겠지.’
284|
285|하지만 지금 돌아간다면 모든 것이 수포로 돌아갈 것이다.
286|
287|그들이 위험을 무릅쓰고 열어 준 하나뿐인 생로(生路)를 포기한다면, 남은 것은 개죽음뿐일 테니까.
288|
289|물론 신분이 신분인 만큼 나처럼 당장 처형시키려고 들지는 않겠지만…… 저 녀석이 돌아가고자 한다면 나는 막을 것이다.
290|

Wonhu snatched the object out of the air. The moment he saw the rough, familiar gourd, a groan escaped him.

[P97]
“This…”

[P98]
There was no mistaking it. His lord, the Beast Miao King, had made this gourd himself and always carried it.

[P99]
“Recognize it?”

[P100]
The voice reached his ears again. Wonhu slowly raised his head.

[P101]
A man stood before him, his white robes stained with blood and filth. His skin was pale enough to match them.

[P102]
“……Baeksang.”

[P103]
Baeksang replied flatly, “How dare a mere warrior speak a Great Chieftain’s name so casually?”

[P104]
“What happened to my lord?”

[P105]
“You’ll find out soon enough.”

[P106]
Swish. Papapat!

[P107]
Baeksang flicked his blood-soaked sleeve. In an instant, more than a hundred Bai warriors emerged from the darkness and surrounded them.

[P108]
*Damn it.*

[P109]
Wonhu drew the broad-bladed saber tucked into his belt.

[P110]
He glanced up. Clouds covered the moon tonight, of all nights. It was a poor night to die, but the darkness was a blessing in one respect.

[P111]
The fugitives would have the advantage if anyone gave chase.

[P112]
*Please be alive. Both of you.*

[P113]
There was only one thing left to do.

[P114]
Wonhu—and every warrior with him—raised their weapons and charged without hesitation.

[P115]
Their roar was too great for fear to find a place among them.

[P116]
* * *

[P117]
Whoooooosh!

[P118]
Cold wind swept over me as the landscape raced past. No people. None of the houses with their unusual shapes. Only thickets.

[P119]
We had left the Outer Palace behind.

[P120]
*But we’re still in the Nanman Beast Palace’s territory. We can’t slow down.*

[P121]
We might have to run without stopping until we rescued the Fire Dragon Pavilion members in the reconnaissance squad. The Nanman Beast Palace’s reach covered this entire unfamiliar land of forests, plains, jungles, and swamps.

[P122]
“Sorry, but I need you to keep going a little longer.”

[P123]
Grrr.

[P124]
Yayul Mok was right: the White Tiger really was a spiritual creature. It seemed to understand me even over the rushing wind. With a low growl, it picked up speed.

[P125]
Papapapat!

[P126]
Its master, tied to its back, was probably another reason it listened to me so well.

[P127]
I watched Yayul Mok sway gently with each bound and sighed.

[P128]
*Yayul Mok.*

[P129]
We had made it out of the Outer Palace, but I hadn’t woken him. More accurately, I hadn’t been able to bring myself to try.

[P130]
*If he wakes up, he’ll find some way to go back.*

[P131]
If he did, everything would be for nothing. Abandoning the one escape route they had risked their lives to open would mean nothing but pointless deaths.

[P132]
Given his position, they probably wouldn’t try to execute him on the spot the way they intended to execute me… but if he wanted to go back, I would stop him.

[P133]
For Yayul Mok. For the Miao warriors fighting for him. And for the Fire Dragon Pavilion members.

[P134]
They could call me selfish. They could curse me and point fingers, say I cared only about my own life.

[P135]
But as fucked up as it was, this was the best choice I had.

[P136]
*Damn it.*

[P137]
I bit down hard on my lip.

[P138]
Within a day at most—perhaps half a day—a net over heaven and earth would be cast across Nanman. We had to get as far away as we could and find the reconnaissance squad before then.

[P139]
*The two tribal chieftains leading the squad are effectively loyal to the Beast Miao King. We might be able to rescue the three of them without much of a fight.*

[P140]
That was the best outcome I could imagine.

[P141]
Dark Heaven’s involvement and Baeksang’s betrayal were certain now. I’d somehow ended up at the center of a massacre I’d never asked for. There was no telling what else might happen.

[P142]
*First, get every Fire Dragon Pavilion member out. After that…*

[P143]
My thoughts broke off.

[P144]
Rustle.

[P145]
The White Tiger stopped dead. It had been running at the front without a moment’s hesitation, but now it would not take another step.

[P146]
“What? What’s wrong?”

[P147]
Grrr.

[P148]
“Your master said to keep going northwest, so…”

[P149]
Grrrr. Sniff, sniff.

[P150]
*What?*

[P151]
It looked in two directions, one after the other. Then it buried its nose in my hand and sniffed, just as it had before we set out.

[P152]
*Wait. Could it be?*

[P153]
At that moment—

[P154]
Ding!

[P155]
> **System**
>
> - A Sudden Quest, **Yohi’s Tracking Scent**, has been generated!

[P156]
As the Quest notification rang in my ears, I remembered the scent pouch I had found at Yohi’s Western Yao Estate.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

The Miao warriors roared with laughter and took turns tipping back the gourd.

[P58]
Nanman people were famous for their love of liquor. With twenty grown men sharing it, their boast that they would leave nothing behind sounded entirely plausible.

[P59]
But…

[P60]
“Ahh, that’s good. Your turn, Big Brother. I left you a few drops out of courtesy.”

[P61]
Wonhu took the gourd at last and let out a short laugh.

[P62]
Slosh.

[P63]
One light shake told him enough. It was not even half empty.

[P64]
The men stood there shamelessly praising the liquor, and he couldn’t help laughing again.

[P65]
“Turns out you’re not mutts. You’re just a pack of blowhards.”

[P66]
“Hm? What’s that supposed to mean?”

[P67]
“Has senility caught up with you already? You’re only in your fifties.”

[P68]
“Enough nonsense. Drink.”

[P69]
At their urging, Wonhu tipped the gourd—not toward his mouth, but toward the weed-covered ground.

[P70]
Trickle.

[P71]
“Don’t begrudge a single drop. If we survive, we’ll sit together and drink all night. If we fall here, we can get drunk after we’re dead.”

[P72]
“……!”

[P73]
“……!”

[P74]
The men watched him with solemn faces. Then their mouths curled into smiles.

[P75]
“Yeah. I like that.”

[P76]
“Big Brother knows what he’s talking about.”

[P77]
“You’ve always been crazier about liquor than martial arts, haven’t you?”

[P78]
Wonhu laughed. So did the Seven Miao Tigers, who had spent their lives alongside him, and the Miao warriors who had volunteered for this dangerous mission.

[P79]
Regrets? Not one.

[P80]
Even if every one of them died here, their only hope would make it out of danger alive.

[P81]
That was why Wonhu could laugh. He thought of the man who had always led from the front, who had sent even his only heir here to set an example.

[P82]
*I’ll gladly take my punishment for disobeying your orders… when we meet in the afterlife, my lord.*

[P83]
Neither the Beast Miao King nor Yayul Mok feared death. They never put their subordinates in front of them as shields, and they never backed away in terror.

[P84]
The Beast Miao King loved the only child he had had late in life more than anything. But if he knew what Wonhu had done, he would scold him. No life was worth more than another.

[P85]
*That’s enough of a reason to give mine.*

[P86]
Wonhu shook the now-empty gourd, watching a few drops fall. He smacked his lips, then called into the darkness around them.

[P87]
“Hey, got any liquor?”

[P88]
A low voice answered.

[P89]
“I thought you were on duty.”

[P90]
“We both know better. Go peel yourself a tiger’s dick and eat it.”

[P91]
Wonhu grinned.

[P92]
Their scheduled shift change was long past, and the waves of energy reaching him from the darkness were strong enough to raise goose bumps.

[P93]
“So? Are you going to share or not?”

[P94]
“I heard the Miao had a liquor-loving monkey. Catch.”

[P95]
Whoosh.

[P96]
Wonhu snatched the object out of the air. The moment he saw the rough, familiar gourd, a groan escaped him.

[P97]
“This…”

[P98]
There was no mistaking it. His lord, the Beast Miao King, had made this gourd himself and always carried it.

[P99]
“Recognize it?”

[P100]
The voice reached his ears again. Wonhu slowly raised his head.

[P101]
A man stood before him, his white robes stained with blood and filth. His skin was pale enough to match them.

[P102]
“……Baeksang.”

[P103]
Baeksang replied flatly, “How dare a mere warrior speak a Great Chieftain’s name so casually?”

[P104]
“What happened to my lord?”

[P105]
“You’ll find out soon enough.”

[P106]
Swish. Papapat!

[P107]
Baeksang flicked his blood-soaked sleeve. In an instant, more than a hundred Bai warriors emerged from the darkness and surrounded them.

[P108]
*Damn it.*

[P109]
Wonhu drew the broad-bladed saber tucked into his belt.

[P110]
He glanced up. Clouds covered the moon tonight, of all nights. It was a poor night to die, but the darkness was a blessing in one respect.

[P111]
The fugitives would have the advantage if anyone gave chase.

[P112]
*Please be alive. Both of you.*

[P113]
There was only one thing left to do.

[P114]
Wonhu—and every warrior with him—raised their weapons and charged without hesitation.

[P115]
Their roar was too great for fear to find a place among them.

[P116]
* * *

[P117]
Whoooooosh!

[P118]
Cold wind swept over me as the landscape raced past. No people. None of the houses with their unusual shapes. Only thickets.

[P119]
We had left the Outer Palace behind.

[P120]
*But we’re still in the Nanman Beast Palace’s territory. We can’t slow down.*

[P121]
We might have to run without stopping until we rescued the Fire Dragon Pavilion members in the reconnaissance squad. The Nanman Beast Palace’s reach covered this entire unfamiliar land of forests, plains, jungles, and swamps.

[P122]
“Sorry, but I need you to keep going a little longer.”

[P123]
Grrr.

[P124]
Yayul Mok was right: the White Tiger really was a spiritual creature. It seemed to understand me even over the rushing wind. With a low growl, it picked up speed.

[P125]
Papapapat!

[P126]
Its master, tied to its back, was probably another reason it listened to me so well.

[P127]
I watched Yayul Mok sway gently with each bound and sighed.

[P128]
*Yayul Mok.*

[P129]
We had made it out of the Outer Palace, but I hadn’t woken him. More accurately, I hadn’t been able to bring myself to try.

[P130]
*If he wakes up, he’ll find some way to go back.*

[P131]
If he did, everything would be for nothing. Abandoning the one escape route they had risked their lives to open would mean nothing but pointless deaths.

[P132]
Given his position, they probably wouldn’t try to execute him on the spot the way they intended to execute me… but if he wanted to go back, I would stop him.

[P133]
For Yayul Mok. For the Miao warriors fighting for him. And for the Fire Dragon Pavilion members.

[P134]
They could call me selfish. They could curse me and point fingers, say I cared only about my own life.

[P135]
But as fucked up as it was, this was the best choice I had.

[P136]
*Damn it.*

[P137]
I bit down hard on my lip.

[P138]
Within a day at most—perhaps half a day—a net over heaven and earth would be cast across Nanman. We had to get as far away as we could and find the reconnaissance squad before then.

[P139]
*The two tribal chieftains leading the squad are effectively loyal to the Beast Miao King. We might be able to rescue the three of them without much of a fight.*

[P140]
That was the best outcome I could imagine.

[P141]
Dark Heaven’s involvement and Baeksang’s betrayal were certain now. I’d somehow ended up at the center of a massacre I’d never asked for. There was no telling what else might happen.

[P142]
*First, get every Fire Dragon Pavilion member out. After that…*

[P143]
My thoughts broke off.

[P144]
Rustle.

[P145]
The White Tiger stopped dead. It had been running at the front without a moment’s hesitation, but now it would not take another step.

[P146]
“What? What’s wrong?”

[P147]
Grrr.

[P148]
“Your master said to keep going northwest, so…”

[P149]
Grrrr. Sniff, sniff.

[P150]
*What?*

[P151]
It looked in two directions, one after the other. Then it buried its nose in my hand and sniffed, just as it had before we set out.

[P152]
*Wait. Could it be?*

[P153]
At that moment—

[P154]
Ding!

[P155]
> **System**
>
> - A Sudden Quest, **Yohi’s Tracking Scent**, has been generated!

[P156]
As the Quest notification rang in my ears, I remembered the scent pouch I had found at Yohi’s Western Yao Estate.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

Wonhu grinned.

[P92]
Their scheduled shift change was long past, and the waves of energy reaching him from the darkness were strong enough to raise goose bumps.

[P93]
“So? Are you going to share or not?”

[P94]
“I heard the Miao had a liquor-loving monkey. Catch.”

[P95]
Whoosh.

[P96]
Wonhu snatched the object out of the air. The moment he saw the rough, familiar gourd, a groan escaped him.

[P97]
“This…”

[P98]
There was no mistaking it. His lord, the Beast Miao King, had made this gourd himself and always carried it.

[P99]
“Recognize it?”

[P100]
The voice reached his ears again. Wonhu slowly raised his head.

[P101]
A man stood before him, his white robes stained with blood and filth. His skin was pale enough to match them.

[P102]
“……Baeksang.”

[P103]
Baeksang replied flatly, “How dare a mere warrior speak a Great Chieftain’s name so casually?”

[P104]
“What happened to my lord?”

[P105]
“You’ll find out soon enough.”

[P106]
Swish. Papapat!

[P107]
Baeksang flicked his blood-soaked sleeve. In an instant, more than a hundred Bai warriors emerged from the darkness and surrounded them.

[P108]
*Damn it.*

[P109]
Wonhu drew the broad-bladed saber tucked into his belt.

[P110]
He glanced up. Clouds covered the moon tonight, of all nights. It was a poor night to die, but the darkness was a blessing in one respect.

[P111]
The fugitives would have the advantage if anyone gave chase.

[P112]
*Please be alive. Both of you.*

[P113]
There was only one thing left to do.

[P114]
Wonhu—and every warrior with him—raised their weapons and charged without hesitation.

[P115]
Their roar was too great for fear to find a place among them.

[P116]
* * *

[P117]
Whoooooosh!

[P118]
Cold wind swept over me as the landscape raced past. No people. None of the houses with their unusual shapes. Only thickets.

[P119]
We had left the Outer Palace behind.

[P120]
*But we’re still in the Nanman Beast Palace’s territory. We can’t slow down.*

[P121]
We might have to run without stopping until we rescued the Fire Dragon Pavilion members in the reconnaissance squad. The Nanman Beast Palace’s reach covered this entire unfamiliar land of forests, plains, jungles, and swamps.

[P122]
“Sorry, but I need you to keep going a little longer.”

[P123]
Grrr.

[P124]
Yayul Mok was right: the White Tiger really was a spiritual creature. It seemed to understand me even over the rushing wind. With a low growl, it picked up speed.

[P125]
Papapapat!

[P126]
Its master, tied to its back, was probably another reason it listened to me so well.

[P127]
I watched Yayul Mok sway gently with each bound and sighed.

[P128]
*Yayul Mok.*

[P129]
We had made it out of the Outer Palace, but I hadn’t woken him. More accurately, I hadn’t been able to bring myself to try.

[P130]
*If he wakes up, he’ll find some way to go back.*

[P131]
If he did, everything would be for nothing. Abandoning the one escape route they had risked their lives to open would mean nothing but pointless deaths.

[P132]
Given his position, they probably wouldn’t try to execute him on the spot the way they intended to execute me… but if he wanted to go back, I would stop him.

[P133]
For Yayul Mok. For the Miao warriors fighting for him. And for the Fire Dragon Pavilion members.

[P134]
They could call me selfish. They could curse me and point fingers, say I cared only about my own life.

[P135]
But as fucked up as it was, this was the best choice I had.

[P136]
*Damn it.*

[P137]
I bit down hard on my lip.

[P138]
Within a day at most—perhaps half a day—a net over heaven and earth would be cast across Nanman. We had to get as far away as we could and find the reconnaissance squad before then.

[P139]
*The two tribal chieftains leading the squad are effectively loyal to the Beast Miao King. We might be able to rescue the three of them without much of a fight.*

[P140]
That was the best outcome I could imagine.

[P141]
Dark Heaven’s involvement and Baeksang’s betrayal were certain now. I’d somehow ended up at the center of a massacre I’d never asked for. There was no telling what else might happen.

[P142]
*First, get every Fire Dragon Pavilion member out. After that…*

[P143]
My thoughts broke off.

[P144]
Rustle.

[P145]
The White Tiger stopped dead. It had been running at the front without a moment’s hesitation, but now it would not take another step.

[P146]
“What? What’s wrong?”

[P147]
Grrr.

[P148]
“Your master said to keep going northwest, so…”

[P149]
Grrrr. Sniff, sniff.

[P150]
*What?*

[P151]
It looked in two directions, one after the other. Then it buried its nose in my hand and sniffed, just as it had before we set out.

[P152]
*Wait. Could it be?*

[P153]
At that moment—

[P154]
Ding!

[P155]
> **System**
>
> - A Sudden Quest, **Yohi’s Tracking Scent**, has been generated!

[P156]
As the Quest notification rang in my ears, I remembered the scent pouch I had found at Yohi’s Western Yao Estate.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
